blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust inside Healthcare & Life Sciences: the operating realities we design for, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Healthcare & Life Sciences, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: PHI concentration and ransomware exposure
Health records carry the highest breach value; ransomware has shuttered hospitals. Legacy devices and third-party vendors widen the surface beyond the IT team's control.
Clinician burden and documentation debt
Physicians spend hours daily on notes, orders and inbox; burnout drives attrition. Documentation AI exists but stalls on integration with the EHR and on compliance sign-off.
Prior authorization and RCM friction
Prior auth, coding and denial management consume staff across payer-provider boundaries. Denials arrive for documentation that existed but was never surfaced.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Under the hood the pattern composes 7 Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust services — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — sequenced by the Dataq Method, with GxP / GCP validation obligations shaping design decisions from the first sprint onward.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation
Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity & Access Modernization
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Cloud Security & Posture Management
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Zero-trust clinical estate
Identity-centric access, device posture and segmentation across hospitals and clinics (ransomware blast radius contained in tabletop evidence)
Medical-device segmentation
IEC 80001-informed zoning for legacy devices with monitoring (unmanaged device surface made visible and controlled)
Clinician documentation time
Down 20-35% with ambient documentation inside the EHR
Radiology reporting turnaround
Down 30-50% with workflow-integrated triage
Prior-authorization cycle time
Down 50-70% with agentic assembly and submission

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GxP / GCP validation and GxP / GCP validation. Computerized-system validation for pharma and trial systems. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
